$comment: Validates _source/erd.json, which is the single source of truth. It is not generated from anything and nothing is generated from it: it exists so that a manuscript missing a bound, a type or a language is refused instead of quietly producing a wrong artifact.
title: gr-scheduler data model source
description: The single source for the data-model figure and its explanation tables. A generator turns this into a StrictDoc markdown document; the prose that explains the tables lives in the specification body, never here.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so an editor validates the file while it is being written.

$comment.description: JSON carries no comments, so notes for whoever edits this file go here. Not rendered.

documents.description: One entry per generated markdown document. Each names the file it is written to; nothing else may be written.

entities.description: Every entity of the data model, in the order they appear in the figure and the tables. ORDER IS LOAD BEARING: the row IDs of the entity table and the column table are positions in this array, so a new entity goes at the END or every later ID shifts.

relations.description: Edges between entities. Order fixes the relation table's row IDs; append at the end. The carry-store edges are NOT listed here: they are derived from the entities whose `carry` is true.

derived.description: Values the document does not store and rebuilds when writing to the exchange partner. Order fixes the derived table's row IDs; append at the end.

printed.description: The fixed prose the generated documents print: the banner, the derived carry rows, and the words a boolean cell shows. ⛔ It used to live inside erd_json_to_md.py, where adding an edition meant editing Python (CR-183). The table HEADINGS sit on their own section, beside the caption they head.

carry.description: The edge and the relation rows drawn for every entity whose `carry` is true. They are derived, so no row of `relations` states them.

words.description: What a cell prints for a value that is not itself prose: a boolean, an absence, and the sentence that carries a decided default. ⚠️ `default_note` holds `{value}` where the value goes. ⚠️ The two separators are prose as well: check 23 caught the same assumption about 「・」 in settings.json -- a mark is not language-neutral just because it is short.

prose.description: PROSE the specification prints, held as a language dictionary. ⚠️ Adding English must be a fill-in, not a rewrite, so every printed sentence sits behind a language key from the start -- the manuscript itself belongs to no language (裁定 ㊹, CR-175). ⛔ NOT every Japanese string: "type" and "nullable" hold Japanese too and are NOT prose. They are a classification whose Japanese wording is a display decision, so wrapping them would burn 「可」 into the manuscript; the generator must print the classification per language instead. The same shape settings.json uses.

en.description: Optional, and nothing reads it yet. It is allowed so that adding an edition is a FILL-IN and not a contract change: the entity "description" is the one place where English is already printed, so that one requires both.

row_comment.description: The comment cell of a plain attribute row: either prose, or a row ID of the settings table, which belongs to no language and is printed as it stands.

document.description: One generated StrictDoc document: where it is written, the UID the specification body links to, and the figures and tables it carries, in order.

file.description: File name under docs/spec/_assets/. kebab-case, per W-11 of table T-006a.

uid.description: The UID the specification body links to. Changing it breaks every [LINK:] that points here.

sections.description: One section per figure or table, in document order.

title.description: The heading text, numbered by hand: '2. 関係'.

block.description: Which generated block fills this section. 'figure' draws the entity diagram F-011 and 'container' the document-shape figure F-010; the other four are the explanation tables.

caption.description: The figure or table number and its title, as the specification numbers them: '表 T-057 — エンティティのあいだの関係'. ⚠️ The number is NOT language-neutral data held beside the prose: 図 and 表 are Japanese words, and the specification prints the caption as one string. A later edition spells its own.

row_prefix.description: First column of every row of this table: 'RL' yields RL-1, RL-2 ... The prefix must not be in use by any other table in the specification; that is checked spec-wide by the markdown checker, not here.

header.description: The heading cells of this table, in printed order. ⭐ The markdown rule under them is DERIVED from how many there are -- writing both was two places to keep in step. A figure section has no header.

name.description: Identifier as it appears in the figure. Upper camel case for an entity, lower camel case for the two document stamps.

description.description: What the entity is. ⚠️ A language dictionary: the Japanese specification prints "ja" in table T-056, and the GRS JSON schema -- which belongs to no language because machines and exchange partners read it -- prints "en" (CR-175).

export.description: Whether the entity is written out to the exchange partner. It is always written to the native JSON.

carry.description: Whether the entity holds a carry store for elements the software does not interpret. Also decides whether an edge to the carry-element entity is drawn.

key_note.description: Overrides the key cell of the entity table when the key cannot be written as a list of column names.

columns.description: ORDER IS LOAD BEARING: the column table numbers its rows across all entities in this order.

type.description: Written for a reader, not for a compiler. A parenthetical part carries the range, the number of values or the unit: '整数（0〜359）'. The figure can only hold one word, so the generator moves the parenthetical next to the origin.

nullable.description: Whether the column may be absent, and what absence means: '可（`null` = 根）'.

json.description: The machine-readable form of "type" and "nullable". It carries what a JSON Schema generator needs and nothing else: the two prose fields stay the ones a reader reads. A range written in "type" appears here as min/max; a rule stated elsewhere in the specification does not.

key.description: Empty for an ordinary column. A key column has its name drawn in bold in the figure.

origin.description: Own: taken from the exchange partner and written back unchanged. Consume: taken in, interpreted, and rebuilt on the way out. GRS: new in this software, no counterpart. Carry: an opaque holder for what is not interpreted.

exchange.description: The element of the exchange partner this column comes from, as a path: 'Task/ActualStart'. A leading ellipsis abbreviates a long path. Empty when the column has no counterpart.

meaning.description: What the column is for, written for a reader. The longest prose in this file and the largest part of a later edition's work.

jsonType.description: A column type a generator can read. "enum" carries "values" once the specification has decided the spellings, and "valuesUndecided" until it has -- a generator must not invent members, so an undecided enum widens to a plain string and gets reported.

format.description: A spelling the specification pins by itself. A date taken from the exchange partner keeps the format it arrived in (EX-4), so it carries no format here.

isDate.description: This column is one table T-058 gives a date or a datetime type. ⚠️ NOT a format: EX-4 keeps whatever spelling the value arrived in, and this says nothing about that. It exists because IV-14 reaches these columns as a set without naming them, so without a marker the roster gets copied by hand and goes stale (F-3, CR-175).

valuesUndecided.description: The specification names the number of members but not their spellings.

default.description: The value the specification uses when the column is absent. ⛔ Only where the specification HAS decided one -- a generator must not invent a default, and a column without this key has none. ⚠️ It is a machine value and belongs to no language, which is why it sits here rather than in the prose of "meaning": the number or spelling is the same in every edition, and holding it twice would let the two disagree. An enum default must be one of "values"; erd_json_to_md.py checks that, because a schema cannot say it.

null.description: Must agree with the "nullable" prose: 可 is true, 否 is false.

jsonTypeElement.description: The element type of a map, an array or an object field. It has no "null" of its own: only a column can be null.

entity.description: Required when kind is "ref": the entity this element repeats.

multiplicity.description: Parent side first, child side second, separated by a box-drawing dash. Only these eight can be drawn.

label.description: What the edge means. The multiplicity is NOT repeated here: the figure draws it as crow's foot notation.

name.description: Name at the exchange partner. Must NOT also be a stored column of the same entity, or the two could disagree.

source.description: What the value is computed from.

container.description: Figure F-010: the shape of the JSON container that holds the entities, drawn as an erDiagram like F-011. Every entity must be placed exactly once -- as the comment of an entity_rows row, as a box of its own, or as a bare node -- and the generator refuses to write anything until that holds. That is what keeps an added entity from slipping past this figure.

boxes.description: A box drawn as a small table.

nodes.description: An entity drawn as a bare labelled node, because it only ever appears nested under another key.

box.description: One erDiagram entity box. Exactly one of `rows`, `entity_rows` or (`entity` with `labels`) says what it contains. `id` is the name drawn on the box: ASCII, because nothing proves the bundled mermaid accepts an alias.

id.description: Node id inside the mermaid figure. Edges use it.

prefixItems.description: The type token. Japanese, and NOT prose: it is the same classification the "type" column of table T-058 holds, so it moves when that one does.
The attribute name, as the JSON spells it.

items.description: Type token, attribute name, comment -- the three cells of one erDiagram attribute. The type must hold no whitespace; the name must be ASCII.

rows.description: Plain attribute rows. Nothing here is checked against the entities, so use it only for keys that are not entities.

items.description: Type token, attribute name, comment -- the three cells of one erDiagram attribute. The type must hold no whitespace; the name must be ASCII.

entity_rows.description: Attribute rows whose COMMENT cell is an entity name. Every name is checked against `entities`.

entity.description: This whole box IS one entity; its rows are that entity's columns, in order.

labels.description: Comment cell per column, in the same order; the type and the name come from the entity itself. The count must equal the entity's column count, so adding a column stops the build until the figure says what it is. The column `meaning` is deliberately not reused: it is prose, too long for a box, and it holds backticks, which break mermaid.

multiplicity.description: Parent side first, child side second. Drawn as crow's foot notation, so it is NOT repeated in the label.

label.description: What the edge means. The multiplicity is not repeated here.

proseList.description: Prose printed as several lines, held per language. The lines are the document's, not the generator's.
